### Part 1 · Before you arrive

Accounts and data only. Nothing here needs software installed at home.

1. **This studio is in the campus Windows room, not our usual classroom.** Check the location on the schedule page before Thursday.
2. Confirm Power BI Desktop opens on the lab machine — it is preinstalled.
3. Download `evm-three-months.xlsx` from the course Drive folder into your `IMSE456` cloud folder.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 2 · What you will have at the end

SA10 — the dashboard, the S-curve plot, ES versus SPI, the anomaly with its evidence, the EAC choice defended
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 3 · Build it yourself — 25 minutes

1. In Colab with pandas, load three months of PV, EV and AC.
2. Compute CV, SV, CPI, SPI, the three EAC families, ETC, VAC and TCPI.
3. Plot the S-curves. The PV curve must be an S and not a line — that is what makes SPI and SPI(t) diverge.
4. Compute Earned Schedule and SPI(t). Compare with SPI.
5. The dataset contains one seeded data-quality anomaly. Find it.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 4 · Now the professional tool — 20 minutes

1. Set the baseline in ProjectLibre, enter actuals, and read its variance columns. Compare the tool's numbers against yours, line by line.
2. In Smartsheet, maintain the same project as a live sheet: baseline columns, actual columns, and a dashboard with metric widgets and a chart widget.
3. <strong>Build the EVM model in Power BI.</strong> Load the Smartsheet export through Power Query. Write CPI, SPI, CV, SV, EAC and TCPI as <em>DAX measures</em>, not as spreadsheet cells — a measure recalculates for whatever period the reader filters to, which is the entire difference between a report and a dashboard.
4. Add a date table and time intelligence so cumulative PV, EV and AC plot as running totals. Publish to the Power BI Service and share a read-only view.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 5 · Where do they disagree? — 15 minutes

Three questions. Which EAC formula is ProjectLibre using, and is that assumption right here — each EAC family makes a different claim about causation, so state the one you adopt. Would your Power BI dashboard have let a sponsor <em>see</em> the seeded anomaly, or does the running total bury it? And which of the three tools would you have caught it in fastest?

Write one paragraph. **This is the graded part** — it is the only thing here a machine cannot check.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 6 · Run the check

Run the `verify()` cell at the end of the notebook. It tests your own outputs against tolerances and
prints a completion code. If it fails, you have found your error while it is still cheap to fix —
that is the point of it. Paste the code into your submission.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 7 · Done looks like — the checklist your neighbour runs on you at minute 65

- [ ] The anomaly is found and traced to a specific period
- [ ] SPI and SPI(t) differ and you can say why
- [ ] CPI and SPI exist as DAX measures that respond to a period filter, not as static numbers
- [ ] the EAC choice is defended as a claim about causation
:::

::: {.part}
